voice: warm, calm, quietly playful English narrator (female, early 30s), close-mic, unhurried

shots.picture: Macro: laptop bezel, webcam lens with a tiny green light; very slow push-in toward the lens; warm living room melts into bokeh.
Raw webcam feed (no UI): the empty room, Miso the cat sitting on the floor, looking around.
shots.vo: But it has no idea what you care about.

shots.picture: Dark navy; the Pulse wordmark with its pulsing cyan dot; subline fades in.
shots.super: Pulse — Tell your camera what to watch for.

shots.picture: Real Pulse Live screen recording in the browser: Maya at her desk in the camera view. The cursor types 'Tell me when Miso jumps on my desk' and adds it. A new watch card slides in; push-in on the precise yes/no question Pulse wrote from that sentence.
shots.vo: Tell it what to watch for, in plain words. Pulse turns your sentence into one precise question, and checks it every second.

shots.picture: Real recording: the feed shows the empty room; Miso crouches, jumps onto the desk and stares into the lens. The watch meter rises, the screen flashes, 'Pulse noticed' toast, and a moment card pops into the feed. Push-in on the card.
shots.sound: music hit + bright chime on the moment

shots.picture: Motion graphic: a filmstrip of webcam frames groups into 2-second clips (4 frames/s). Each clip passes a small 'fast model' gate that answers yes/no bars for every watch (cat 0.62, water 0.03, thumbs 0.01). A likely clip lights up and travels to a larger 'second look' model (cloud) which stamps it confirmed; a look-alike clip is stamped dismissed. Counter: real numbers from the recorded run.
shots.vo: Every second, a fast model reads the last two seconds of video and answers yes or no, for each thing you asked. Only when something looks likely does a bigger model take a second look.
shots.sound: ticks on each clip, low whoosh on the hand-off

shots.picture: Two quick real recordings: 'when I drink water' -> Maya sips -> moment card; 'when I give a thumbs-up' -> thumbs-up -> moment card.
shots.vo: A sip of water. A thumbs-up. Whatever you care about.

shots.picture: Real recording: earlier, Maya set her keys (mustard-yellow tag) on the desk and left. Now 'Where did I leave my keys?' is typed in the Ask box; Pulse answers in a sentence with the evidence frame. Push-in on the answer and the frame.
shots.vo: And because it was paying attention, you can just ask.

shots.picture: A clean phone mockup plays the real 9:16 reel Pulse made of the cat moment (looping); the 1080x1350 moment card slides beside it; a share sheet rises.
shots.vo: Every moment becomes a card, or a clip, made to share.

shots.picture: Maya curled up on the sofa laughing at her phone (screen faces her).
A rolling 3-minute ring of frames: old frames fade to nothing as new ones arrive; only a few moment cards stay pinned. A 'Forget everything' button is pressed and the cards dissolve.
shots.vo: Frames stay in memory for three minutes, then they're gone. Only your moments are kept.

shots.picture: Miso sits on the desk beside the glowing laptop at golden hour, then turns his head to the camera and blinks slowly.
shots.vo: Pulse. Tell your camera what matters.

shots.picture: Pulse wordmark; 'Open it in your browser'; small honest footnote: camera feeds generated for this demo; detections, cards and answers are live Pulse output.
